title: Application Load Balancer Reports Unhealthy Targets
symptom: ALB target group shows all registered targets with Status: 'Unhealthy' and reason 'Target.Timeout' or 'Target.ResponseCodeMismatch'.
initial_observations: ALB returns HTTP 502 or 503 to web clients.
Targets are in running state in EC2 console.
environment: AWS ALB routing to EC2 target group.

possible_causes.cause: Target Security Group blocks traffic coming from the ALB Security Group
possible_causes.evidence_needed: Health check reason is Target.Timeout; EC2 SG has no inbound rule for ALB SG.
possible_causes.remediation: Add an inbound rule to target SG permitting traffic on target port with source set to ALB Security Group ID.

possible_causes.cause: Health check path returns HTTP status outside the configured matcher (e.g. 404 or 301 vs expected 200)
possible_causes.remediation: Update Target Group health check path to a valid endpoint or update application routing.

investigation_steps.title: Query Target Health and Specific Reason Codes
investigation_steps.explanation: Retrieve specific health check failure reason for each target.

investigation_steps.title: Test Health Check Endpoint Directly from Within VPC
investigation_steps.explanation: Observe the exact HTTP response code and headers returned by the target.
investigation_steps.what_to_look_for: HTTP response code vs Target Group matcher setting.

prevention: Dedicate a lightweight `/healthz` endpoint returning HTTP 200 that does not require database access or authentication.
Use Security Group reference rules instead of static CIDR ranges.
